ui.demo: The pictures were taken on demonstration data, in French.
ui.deniedTitle: This guide is not for your account
ui.denied: This guide describes tools your account does not have. Open the one that matches your role.

voter.name: Voter
voter.lead: Voting takes a few minutes, on a computer or a phone. You have no account: your slip carries a personal code, and that is all you need.

before.title: Before it opens
before.lead: If the election has not started yet, the page says so and counts down to the opening.
steps: Open the voting address written on your slip, or scan the QR code.
Read the election title and the time left before it opens.
Come back at the time shown: the page does not ask for a code until voting is open.
legend: The election title and the institution.
before.tip: You can leave the page open: it moves to the code entry by itself.

code.title: Enter your code
code.lead: Your personal code is on the slip the institution gave you, or in the email you received.
steps: Open the voting page. If you scanned the QR code or clicked the link you received, the code is already filled in: go to the next step.
Type your code in the ten boxes: five characters, a dash, five characters. Upper or lower case, with or without the dash.
Press “Continue”.
legend: The election title: check it is the right one.
The ten boxes of the code.
code.tip: A code never contains the characters 0, O, 1, I or L: nothing can be mistaken.

identity.title: Check that it is you
identity.lead: After the code, the page shows your name and your group so you can confirm the slip is yours.
steps: Read your name and your class or group.
Look at the list of elections you vote in: it depends on your group.
If all is right, press “Yes, it is me”.
If it is not you, press “It is not me”: the session is closed and the slip stays untouched.
legend: The first ballot you take part in.

ballot.title: Choose a candidate
ballot.lead: Each ballot has its own page. Candidates are shown with their photo, party and slogan.
steps: Look at the progress bar: it shows which ballot you are on.
Touch the card of the candidate you choose. It is highlighted and the name appears at the bottom.
To change your mind, touch another card.
Press “Next”. The button only turns on after you choose.
legend: The progress: the current ballot among all those that concern you.
A chosen candidate: the name is repeated at the bottom of the screen.
The blank vote, when the ballot allows it.
ballot.tip: Nothing is recorded until you confirm at the very end.

blank.title: Vote blank
blank.lead: When the ballot allows it, you may choose nobody: that is the blank vote.
steps: Touch the “Blank vote” box under the candidates. The candidates are deselected.
To undo it, touch it again or choose a candidate.
Press “Next”.
legend: The reminder of what you chose.

several.title: Choose several candidates
several.lead: Some ballots elect several people, for example two members of a committee.
steps: Read the instruction at the top: “Choose 2 candidates”, for example.
Touch each candidate you want. The counter shows how many you have chosen.
When you reach the number of seats, the other cards lock. To change, first remove a candidate.
Press “Next”.
legend: Go back to the previous ballot.

review.title: Read your ballot again
review.lead: Before recording, a page sums up your choice for each ballot.
steps: Read your choices, ballot by ballot.
To fix one, press “Edit” next to that ballot: you go back to it, then continue.
When all is right, press “Confirm my vote”.
legend: Confirm: all ballots are recorded in one go.
review.tip: A confirmed vote is final: it can be neither changed nor cast again.

done.title: Your vote is recorded
done.lead: A confirmation page gives the date and time. It does not show your choices: the vote is secret.
steps: Check the confirmation message and the time.
You can close the page. On a shared device it returns to the code entry by itself after a few seconds, for the next person.
legend: The date and time of your vote.

phone.title: On a phone
phone.lead: The whole path works on a small screen, including an entry-level phone.
steps: Open the link or scan the QR code with the phone’s camera.
Follow the same steps: code, check, ballots, review, confirmation.
Candidate cards stack up; scroll to see them all. The “Back” and “Next” buttons stay at the bottom of the screen.
legend: The button to continue, always visible.

problems.title: If something goes wrong
problems.lead: The messages say what is happening, without jargon.
steps: “Invalid code”: check the characters, especially 2/Z, 5/S, 8/B. Type it again carefully.
Several failed tries in a row block entry for a few minutes: wait, then try again.
“You have already voted”: your vote is recorded, there is nothing to redo.
Lost or unreadable code: ask the person who runs the election, they can issue a new one.
Your session lasts 15 minutes at most: if it expires, enter your code again; nothing had been recorded.
legend: The error message, in plain words.

closed.title: After it closes
closed.lead: When voting is over, the page says so.
steps: The message “Voting has ended” replaces the code entry.
If the institution published the results, a link takes you there without an account.
If voting is interrupted (a suspension, for example), the page says so: try again later, votes already recorded are kept.

manager.name: Manager
manager.lead: Prepare, open and follow an election: ballots, candidates, voters, codes, turnout, results. The pictures show the real screens.

signin.title: Sign in
signin.lead: You get an invitation by email (or, on a school installation, a temporary password).
steps: Open your institution’s site address.
Type your email address and your password.
Press “Sign in”. If two-factor authentication is on, type the code from your app.
Forgot your password: “Forgot your password?” sends a reset link.
legend: Create an institution (for a new institution only).

dashboard.title: The dashboard
dashboard.lead: This is the landing page: the open election and its turnout, what is left to do, key figures.
steps: Read the welcome banner and the current election.
Use the shortcuts to create an election or invite someone.
Open the menu on the left to move between sections; the “Go to” search finds a page, an election or a voter.
The round button at the top right opens your account, the guide and sign out.
legend: The open election, with live turnout.
dashboard.tip: Any page is at most three clicks from another.

create.title: Create an election
create.lead: An election has a title, dates and a language. The rest (ballots, candidates, voters) comes next.
steps: In “Elections”, press “New election”.
Give a clear title, for example “Student council election 2026”.
Choose the start and end date and time. Times are in the election’s time zone (Haiti by default).
Choose the language of the voting screens, then save: the election is a draft.
create.tip: The end must be after the start. A draft can be edited or deleted freely.

election.title: An election’s page
election.lead: The whole election is run from here: the steps, the checklist and the actions.
steps: Read the banner: title, status (draft, scheduled, open, closed), dates.
Follow the five steps: ballots, candidates, voters, codes, scheduling.
The checklist says what blocks opening and what is only a warning.
Change dates or language with “Edit”.
legend: The election banner and its status.

ballots.title: Ballots
ballots.lead: A ballot is a seat to fill: president, class delegate, committee… An election can have several.
steps: Open “Ballots” and press “Add a ballot”.
Give the title, the number of seats and say whether the blank vote is allowed.
Choose the scope: all voters, or only some groups (the 4th grade, for example).
Reorder ballots by dragging: this is the order the voter sees.
legend: The number of seats to fill.
The scope: a ballot reserved for groups.
ballots.tip: A group ballot with fewer than 5 voters triggers a warning: the result could reveal an individual vote.

candidates.title: Candidates and parties
candidates.lead: Each ballot has its candidates; a party is optional.
steps: On the ballot card, press “Add a candidate”.
Type the first name, the last name and the sex (it picks the avatar while there is no photo).
Add a party, a slogan, a short presentation and a photo if you wish (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 5 MB at most).
Look at the preview: it is what the voter will see. Save, or “Save and add another”.
candidates.tip: The order can be manual or shuffled for each voter; choose it in the election settings.

voters.title: Voters and groups
voters.lead: A voter record holds a name, a group, and optionally an identifier, an email, a phone. No date of birth.
steps: Open “Voters”.
Add a voter with “Add”, or import a file (next step), or take those of a past election with “Copy from an election”.
Search by name; filter by group, code status or “has voted”.
Groups can be renamed and merged from their card.
legend: Take the voters of an earlier election.
voters.tip: You can see whether a voter has voted and when, never for whom.

import.title: Import a voter file
import.lead: For a long list, import a CSV or Excel file (up to 10,000 rows).
steps: Download the template (CSV or Excel) and fill it in: full name, group, identifier, email, phone.
Drop the file in the area provided.
Check the column mapping, then the preview: each row is checked (missing name, invalid email, duplicate).
Confirm: valid rows are imported; refused rows are returned in an error file.
legend: The area to drop the file in.
import.tip: Nothing is imported before you confirm.

codes.title: Voting codes
codes.lead: Each voter gets a personal ten-character code. It is shown once: the system keeps only its fingerprint.
steps: Open “Codes”.
Press “Generate codes”: for all voters, a group or one person.
Choose how to hand them out: slips to print (PDF, one page per class), email, or a file you distribute yourself.
Download the files right away: they are encrypted and deleted when the election closes.
legend: The summary: how many voters have a code, how many do not.
Send by email (the number of messages is announced and must be confirmed).
A lost code: a new one is issued, the old one is cancelled.
codes.tip: A code cannot be shown again: only reissued. Reissuing is refused if the person has already voted.

schedule.title: Schedule the election
schedule.lead: Scheduling freezes ballots and candidates; opening then happens by itself at the start time.
steps: On the election page, read the checklist: blockers must be fixed.
Read the warnings (a group with no voter, a voter with no ballot) and decide.
Press “Schedule the election” and accept the warnings if you stand by them.
Until it opens, you can go back to draft to fix things.
legend: The steps: everything must be done.

turnout.title: Follow turnout
turnout.lead: While voting runs, you see who takes part, never the results.
steps: Open “Turnout” from the election page.
Read the live percentage, the chart by hour and the breakdown by group.
Use the list of people who have not voted to remind them; export it as CSV or Excel.
If needed, push back the end of voting with “Extend”.
legend: The people who have not voted yet.
turnout.tip: No vote count is visible before closing, to anyone, not even the platform.

close.title: Close
close.lead: Voting ends by itself at the end time. You can also close it earlier.
steps: On the election page, press “Close now”.
Read what will happen: no more votes will be accepted.
Type the exact election title to confirm.
Press “Close”: the results become visible to you.

results.title: Read the results
results.lead: After closing, each ballot shows votes, percentages, blank votes and the winner or winners.
steps: Read the turnout and, for each ballot, the winners.
Check the verification: the number of ballots must equal the number of eligible voters who voted.
In case of a tie for the last seat, the system reports it without deciding; you can open a second round with the tied candidates.
Add a public note to a ballot if needed.
results.tip: The result of a general ballot is never broken down by group.

publication.title: Publish
publication.lead: Publishing creates a public page, readable without an account, at a stable address.
steps: In the “Publication” card, press “Publish”.
Choose what the public sees: the full figures, or only the winners and turnout.
Confirm. The page is online at once and can be unpublished whenever you want.

published.title: Share and download
published.lead: Once published, you have the public address, the PDF report and the image to share.
steps: Copy the public address or share it on WhatsApp, Facebook or X.
Download the official report as a PDF.
To take the page down, press “Unpublish”; you can then archive the election.

public.title: What the public sees
public.lead: The public page is made to be shared: a phone is enough.
steps: The visitor sees the turnout and the winners (and the figures, if you chose so).
They can share on WhatsApp, Facebook, X or copy the link.
The institution’s page lists all its published elections.

account.title: My account and two-factor authentication
account.lead: Your password and an extra protection are set in “My account”.
steps: Open your menu (round button at the top right), then “My account”.
Change your password: the old one, then the new one (at least 12 characters).
Turn on two-factor authentication: a code from your app will be asked at each sign-in.
Keep the eight recovery codes somewhere safe.

limits.title: What a manager cannot do
limits.lead: Some actions are reserved for the institution’s owner.
steps: Manage users (invite, remove, reset).
Read the institution’s audit log.
Delete the institution.
For everything else (elections, ballots, voters, codes, results), your role is enough.
legend: The note that explains it on the institution page.

owner.name: Owner
owner.lead: You are responsible for the institution: its profile, its team, its log, its security. The “Manager” guide describes the rest.

register.title: Create the institution
register.lead: On an online installation, the first person creates the institution and becomes its owner.
steps: Open the “Create an institution” page.
Type the institution’s name, your name, your email and a password of at least 12 characters.
Press “Create my institution”: you land on the dashboard.
legend: Your password, with a strength indicator.
register.tip: On the “school” edition installed on a local server, there is no email: the installer creates your account and a temporary password to change at first sign-in.

verify.title: Verify the email address
verify.lead: Before scheduling an election, your address must be verified.
steps: A banner at the top of the dashboard reminds you.
Open the email you received and click the link.
No email? “Resend” sends a new one.

institution.title: The institution profile
institution.lead: Name, type, logo, address, contact details, time zone and default language.
steps: Open “Institution” in the menu.
Fill in the profile: the name and logo appear on voting pages and results.
Choose the time zone (Port-au-Prince by default) and the language.
Save.
legend: The public address of the institution page.

team.title: Invite someone
team.lead: An owner can invite other owners and managers.
steps: In “Institution”, press “Invite”.
Type the person’s email.
Choose the role: manager (elections, voters, codes) or owner (everything).
Press “Send the invitation”.
team.tip: On the school edition (no email), you create the person yourself: a temporary password is shown once, to hand to them.

invitation.title: Follow invitations and the team
invitation.lead: Each invitation has a status; each member a role.
steps: Pending invitations appear with their status and expiry date.
Cancel those that are no longer needed.
For a member, you can change the role, reset their password or two-factor authentication, or remove them.
The institution always keeps at least one owner.

audit.title: The audit log
audit.lead: Every important action is recorded: who, what, when, from which address. Nobody can erase it.
steps: Open “Log” in the menu.
Filter by person, election, action or dates.
Export as CSV or Excel to archive it or show it.

twofactor.title: Turn on two-factor authentication
twofactor.lead: Recommended for every owner: a stolen password is no longer enough.
steps: In “My account”, press “Turn on”.
Type your password.
Scan the QR code with an authenticator app, or type the key by hand.
Type the six-digit code shown, then confirm.
Note the eight recovery codes and tick “I have saved them”.
legend: The backup key, to type by hand.

public.title: Your public page
public.lead: Your institution has a public page that lists published elections.
steps: On the “Institution” page, the public address is shown.
Copy it to put on your site or share it.
Open it to see what the public sees.

platform.name: Platform administrator
platform.lead: You manage the platform’s institutions. You never see votes, codes or voters’ contact details.

signin.title: Sign in
signin.lead: The account is created by the server operator with the administration command.
steps: Open the site’s sign-in page.
Type your address and your password.
Type the two-factor code (required for this role).

list.title: The list of institutions
list.lead: Each institution is a card: status, number of elections, owner.
steps: Search by name with the search bar.
Filter by status: active or suspended.
Read the card’s name, status and figures.
Use “Suspend” or “Act as the owner” from the card.
legend: Act as the owner, to help.

suspend.title: Suspend an institution
suspend.lead: A suspension blocks sign-in and pauses the votes in progress.
steps: Press “Suspend” on the card.
Write the reason: it is shown to users and sent to owners.
Confirm. Open elections are paused: voters see a “voting suspended” page.
“Reactivate” restores everything; elections resume where they were.

impersonate.title: Act as the owner
impersonate.lead: To help an institution, you can open its owner session.
steps: Press “Act as the owner” on the card.
A banner reminds you at all times that you act for them.
Press “End” to go back to your platform screen.
Every action is written to the institution’s log, with your name.

twofactor.title: Two-factor authentication
twofactor.lead: It is required for the platform administrator.
steps: At first sign-in, the screen asks you to turn it on.
Scan the QR code with an authenticator app.
Keep the recovery codes away from the server.
If lost, the operator resets it with “votectl 2fa reset”.

limits.title: What you cannot do
limits.lead: These limits are deliberate: they protect the secrecy of the vote.
steps: See a vote, an access code or a voter’s contact details.
Read the vote counts before an election is closed.
Change an institution’s content without acting in its name (and so without a trace).

install.name: Installation
install.lead: Put VoteSystem into service on a computer or a server. Three ways, depending on hardware and connection.

choose.title: Which installation to choose?
steps: A Linux server in the institution, with no internet: the Linux “school” installer (Debian 12 or 13, Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04). No email; accounts are created by the installer.
A Windows 11 computer in the institution: the Windows installer (see the next section).
An online server with a domain name: the Docker “online” installer, with automatic HTTPS and email.
choose.tip: All three provide the “votectl” command for daily operation.

linux.title: Install on Linux (school)
linux.lead: One script, no Docker: it installs the services, a database and the site.
steps: Download the version’s archive and its checksum file.
Check the checksum, then unpack the archive.
Run the installer as an administrator and answer the questions (or add --yes to accept the proposed values).
At the end, read the summary: site address, ports, files written.
linux.tip: The installer tests space, memory and ports, takes the next free port if 80 is busy, and offers to open the port in the firewall.

windows.title: Install on Windows
windows.lead: A Windows installation is planned; its method depends on the tests under way.
steps: This section will be completed with the chosen method as soon as the tests are done.
Meanwhile, use the Linux server or the online version.

docker.title: Install online with Docker
docker.lead: For a public server with a single domain name.
steps: The domain name must already point to the server; ports 80 and 443 must be free.
Download the version’s archive, check the checksum, unpack.
Run the installer as an administrator: it asks its questions once (domain, SMTP email, platform administrator’s address).
Behind another proxy, answer “yes” to “another proxy will do the HTTPS”: VoteSystem then listens locally.

first.title: First sign-in
first.lead: The installer writes two files in the folder of the person who ran sudo.
steps: Open “votesystem-identifiants.txt”: the addresses and the temporary passwords.
Copy “votesystem-cle-audit-A-EMPORTER.txt” to a USB key or another computer, then delete it from the server: it is the audit private key and must not stay on the machine.
Open the site address and sign in: you are asked to change the temporary password before anything else.
Turn on two-factor authentication for the owner and the administrator.

daily.title: Daily operation with votectl
daily.lead: The “votectl” command does the day-to-day work, without touching vote data.
steps: votectl status: the state of the services and of the disk.
votectl user list, user reset-password, 2fa reset: the accounts.
votectl owner create and admin create: new accounts.
votectl logs [service]: the logs.

update.title: Update
update.lead: An update keeps the data and goes back if it fails.
steps: Download the new version and unpack it.
Run the update command: a backup is made first.
If the migration step fails, the previous version is put back in service automatically.
update.tip: The first command is for the school edition, the second for the online edition.

backup.title: Back up and restore
backup.lead: A backup is a checked archive: database and pictures.
steps: An automatic backup runs every night (school edition).
To make one on demand, run the command below.
Regularly copy the archives to an external disk.
To restore, use “votectl restore” with the file: try it once before you need it.
backup.tip: The audit private key is never part of a backup.

problems.title: If there is a problem
steps: The site does not answer: “votectl status” shows which service is stopped.
The port is taken: run the installer again, it picks the next one and writes it in the summary.
Voters cannot reach the site: check the server firewall and that devices are on the same network.
Lost password: “votectl user reset-password” generates a temporary one.

uninstall.title: Uninstall
uninstall.lead: Uninstalling removes the services; the data is deleted only on request.
steps: Run the uninstall command: services and the firewall rule are removed, the data stays.
With --purge-data, the data is deleted too: use it only after a backup copied elsewhere.
